name: Certipy
what: A Python toolkit for enumerating and testing Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS). It finds misconfigured certificate templates and enrollment paths that can escalate a low-privileged domain user to high privilege (the ESC-class issues from SpecterOps research).
when: On every AD engagement where AD CS is present, and for purple-team validation after you harden templates, enrollment permissions and ESC6/ESC8-style relay paths.
example: Install with Python 3.12+: `pip install certipy-ad` (command is `certipy`).
Against an approved lab domain, enumerate with a domain user: `certipy find -u analyst@contoso.lab -p 'REDACTED' -dc-ip 10.10.10.10 -vulnerable -stdout`.
Triage flagged ESC findings with the Certipy wiki privilege-escalation notes and your AD CS hardening baseline.
Open tickets for over-permissive templates, enrollment rights on Domain Controllers, and HTTP enrollment endpoints that allow NTLM relay; re-run after fixes.
pitfalls: Requesting certificates or abusing templates outside a signed scope can create lasting privileged credentials; stick to find/enumerate until abuse is approved.
BloodHound CE and Certipy complement each other; export Certipy data into BloodHound when you need graph paths.
Python version matters: current releases expect 3.12+.
